archetype.name: Game Manager (short-area, sack-averse)
archetype.definition: In his third year in Sean Payton's offense, Nix lives at or behind the line of scrimmage, protects the ball and the sack column, and leans on a top-tier defense to keep games close.

report.headline: Sacks and picks under control, but third downs are sinking the passing game
report.take:
Nix is not the passer he was billed as after 2025, at least not yet this season. His intended air yards sit at 6.19 and he throws 2.84 yards short of the sticks on average. Of his 250 charted attempts, 71 have gone behind the line and another 120 inside nine yards. The result is a low-variance, low-ceiling passing line: 5.97 yards per attempt (39th of 47), -0.012 EPA per dropback (28th) and a CPOE of -2.44. That is a real step back from a 2025 in which he threw for 231.2 yards a game. It is not a collapse, though, because the floor plays that sink most young quarterbacks are missing. His sack rate of 3.8% ranks 7th, only 17.3% of his pressures become sacks (5th), and his interception rate of 1.2% sits well under the 2.3% league average.

The season is really two stories split by down. On early downs the offense works: short throws (0-9 air yards) return +0.159 EPA with a CPOE of +3.2, and in the red zone he has 8 touchdowns at +0.25 EPA a play. Then third down arrives with an average of 7.7 yards to go, and everything breaks. He's at -0.516 EPA per play, a 48% completion rate and a 23.1% conversion rate. Those 78 third-down plays add up to -40.2 EPA, a hole far deeper than his entire season's dropback total of -0.9. So outside of third down he has been comfortably positive, and on third down he has been one of the league's worst. Long yardage forces him to the intermediate level and the middle of the field. Those are exactly the throws he is missing: 40% completions and a -12.5 CPOE at 10-19 yards, a -15.9 CPOE over the middle.

The career context matters here. His CPOE has slid each year, from +0.56 as a rookie to -1.2 in 2025 to -2.44 now. His rushing has also shrunk every season, from 430 yards to 356 to a 242-yard pace, and designed runs this year average 1.88 yards with a 31.3% stuff rate. The accuracy dip is a trend, not an eight-game blip. The sack avoidance is also long-standing (pressure-to-sack ranked 10th and 7th the last two years), so that part is who he is. Behind it sits a line that has allowed the league's lowest hit rate, which helps.

The last three weeks are better: +0.063 EPA per dropback, no interceptions, three wins. That is mostly turnover-free football rather than a new level of downfield accuracy; his CPOE in that stretch is unchanged at -2.5. The bigger near-term issue is that RJ Harvey, his most efficient target at +0.216 EPA per target, is on IR until December. That takes away the one checkdown option who turned short throws into gains.

strengths.title: Avoids sacks and interceptions
strengths.body: Nix gets the ball out or gets out of trouble. He converts only 17.3% of pressures into sacks and has thrown no interceptions over his last five games. Denver's line allowing the league's lowest hit rate helps, but his pressure-to-sack ranks of 10th and 7th in prior seasons show the trait is his. Expect it to hold.

strengths.title: Efficient on short, on-time throws
strengths.body: Between the line and nine air yards he completes 67.5% with a +3.2 CPOE and +0.159 EPA a throw. These are rhythm throws on schedule, the backbone of Payton's early-down plan. This is a repeatable skill, and it is why the offense moves when it stays ahead of the chains.

strengths.title: Finishing in the red zone
strengths.body: He has 8 red-zone touchdown passes at +0.25 EPA a play with a positive CPOE. That is nearly all of his passing touchdowns, and it is what keeps his fantasy line respectable despite thin yardage. The compressed field suits his short-area game, but a rate this efficient on 36 plays will likely cool somewhat.

concerns.title: Third down is a disaster
concerns.body: He's at -0.516 EPA a play, completing 48% and converting 23.1% of third downs. Those plays add up to -40.2 EPA, more than enough to drag an otherwise positive season below average. The cause is structural: third-and-long demands the intermediate and middle-of-field throws he is missing badly. Some of this should regress toward his prior norms, but it won't flip without better accuracy past ten yards.

concerns.title: Accuracy sliding for three years
concerns.body: His CPOE has dropped every season and sits at -2.44 now. Throws of 10-19 air yards carry a -12.5 CPOE with 2 interceptions. Completion rate is down 3.8 points from last year, and the volume of throws behind the line (-0.238 EPA, -16.9 total) suggests the staff is designing around it. This looks like a real limitation, not noise.

concerns.title: Losing Harvey, keeping Sutton's struggles
concerns.body: Harvey (knee, IR until about December 6) was his best target by EPA, and Courtland Sutton has been a drain at -0.145 EPA per target. Without Harvey, more of the short game shifts to Waddle and Engram. The screen-and-checkdown floor gets thinner for the next month.

trend.note: After a -14.4 EPA opener and two negative games in Weeks 5-6, he has posted positive passing EPA in each of the last two. Over the last three he is at +0.063 per dropback with no picks. The gain comes from cleaner ball security rather than better accuracy, so it's a modest climb, not a breakout.

nextGame.headline: A clean pocket and thin secondary set up a solid day
nextGame.body:
Carolina's pass rush is among the league's weakest: 30th in hit rate and 27th in sack rate. For a quarterback whose game is built on staying on schedule, that should mean more third-and-manageable and less of the third-and-long that has wrecked him. The Panthers' pass defense ranks 18th by EPA. They are 3rd in limiting explosive passes, though, which caps the upside of the few deep shots he takes. Their WR1 coverage has been stingy (4th in EPA allowed), a tougher look for Waddle, while tight ends have feasted at 0.42 EPA a target (27th). That points to Engram as the soft spot. Denver is a 3-point favorite with a 43.5 total, and that script suits the Broncos' defense-first approach.

Availability tilts his way. Carolina has corner Akayleb Evans on IR and corner Will Lee III questionable with a hamstring. Linebacker Jaelan Phillips is listed out after playing 64% of snaps, which thins an already weak rush. On Denver's side, Harvey's absence removes Nix's most efficient outlet, so expect the short game to run through Waddle and Engram rather than the backfield.

keyMatchups.title: Nix vs. a passive pass rush
keyMatchups.body: Carolina rarely hits or sacks quarterbacks, and Nix already avoids sacks better than almost anyone. A clean pocket should give him time to work intermediate routes that pressure has made harder. That makes this a real chance to improve his third-down numbers.

keyMatchups.title: Engram against a leaky TE defense
keyMatchups.body: Tight ends have produced 0.42 EPA a target against Carolina, near the bottom of the league, and score above their averages against it. Engram has been below average for Nix (-0.081 EPA a target). This is a good spot for that connection to turn over the middle, where Nix has struggled.

keyMatchups.title: Waddle into stingy WR1 coverage
keyMatchups.body: Waddle is his most-targeted receiver, but Carolina has held WR1s to 0.07 EPA a target (4th) and under their usual scoring. The injured corner room could soften that. Still, Nix may need to spread the ball rather than force it to his top option.

nextGame.watch: His third-down conversion rate: with Carolina's weak rush, anything near a normal rate means the clean-pocket matchup is paying off.

restOfSeason.body:
The sack avoidance, low interception rate and short-area efficiency have held across three seasons and should stay. The third-down collapse is extreme enough that some recovery toward his prior norms is likely, and that alone would lift his efficiency back toward league average. What won't change quickly is the downfield accuracy trend or the shrinking rushing role. Expect yardage to stay modest, roughly 180-235 a game, with touchdowns tied heavily to red-zone trips. His red-zone rate will probably cool a bit.

Harvey's absence until about December thins the short game, and Sutton's inefficiency limits the second option. A defense that ranks near the top keeps games close, which caps passing volume but protects his floor. He projects as a steady, low-ceiling starter rather than the volume passer of 2025, unless the intermediate throws come back.
swingFactors: Third-down efficiency regressing toward his career norms
Harvey's return from IR in December

confidence.note: The traits are clear and backed by his career, but eight games and a 78-play third-down split leave room for regression.
